bedrock_taxonomy_scope: Full destination taxonomy, independently of the Laya shortlist.
methodology: Freeze this protocol, prompts and authored labels before the first benchmark prediction.
The 0.95 threshold was selected after observing the existing regression set. Regression results are exploratory, not independent validation.

Fresh products use new names and wording but familiar category concepts and the same fictional taxonomies. They were authored after prior errors were known; this is a prospective diagnostic set, not an independent commercial holdout.
Run live Laya and Bedrock once for every product/destination, with no accuracy-driven retries or prompt edits. Never send expected labels or prior predictions to Bedrock.

Derive the cascade from paired recorded calls, accepting valid non-unmatched Laya choices at or above the fixed threshold. All other cases use the corresponding Bedrock result without a second paid call.

Bedrock can return mapped, no_match or insufficient_information. Non-mapped decisions normalize to unmatched for existing exact-label scoring, but remain unresolved products rather than completed mappings.
Record successful token usage, API wall time, local Laya wall/model time, raw outputs and hashes. Errors remain in the denominator.
Cascade latency and token savings are calculated from the paired calls; this does not benchmark a deployed cascade or concurrent throughput.
Report datasets separately. Multiple destination decisions share products and taxonomies and are not statistically independent.
Cost estimates cover Standard ON DEMAND Bedrock inference only, excluding Laya hardware, idle capacity, networking, human review, taxes and any failed calls with unknown usage.
Keep all failures visible and do not relax existing Laya quality gates.
